content.title: Toyota Recalls 550,000 Highlander SUVs Over Second-Row Seat Defect
content.text: If you use one of Toyota’s most popular three-row SUVs as your daily family hauler, you need to pay attention to a massive new safety alert. Toyota is officially recalling approximately 550,000 Highlander and Highlander Hybrid models across the United States due to a concerning defect that could leave second-row passengers vulnerable in a crash. The Unlocked Seat Issue The sweeping recall affects certain 2021 through 2024 model-year Toyota Highlander and Highlander Hybrid vehicles. According to the automaker, the safety risk stems from a faulty mechanism inside the second-row seating. Toyota discovered that the recliner assemblies in the second-row seats may fail to fully lock into place after a passenger adjusts the seat back. While a loose seat back might just seem like a minor annoyance during a standard daily commute, it becomes a severe hazard in the event of an accident. If the seat back is not securely locked into its proper position, it may fail to adequately restrain the occupant during a collision. Toyota warns that this defect significantly increases the risk of injury, particularly in high-speed crashes. The Free Dealership Fix Fortunately, Toyota is already preparing a permanent remedy for the affected SUVs. Once the final fix is rolled out to service centers, authorized Toyota dealers will inspect the seats and replace the faulty return springs inside the recliner assemblies with improved, redesigned components. As with all official safety recalls, this repair will be performed at absolutely no cost to the owner. Toyota stated that it plans to begin mailing official notification letters to the owners of the 550,000 involved vehicles by early May 2026. How to Check Your Highlander’s VIN Because this recall impacts over half a million vehicles, you shouldn’t wait for a letter in the mail to find out if your family SUV is affected. You can easily check your vehicle’s status right now by visiting Toyota.com/recall or the official National Highway Traffic Safety Administration database at nhtsa.gov/recalls. Simply enter your SUV’s 17-digit Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) or your license plate information to see if you need to schedule a service appointment. If you have any additional questions about the repair process or the safety of your seats, you can also contact the Toyota Brand Engagement Center directly at 1-800-331-4331.
